t: Above you is Nelson's Column, the monument at the heart of Trafalgar Square. It commemorates Horatio Nelson's decisive victory over the combined French and Spanish navies at Trafalgar, where he was killed by a French sniper. William Railton designed it, and it was built between 1840 and 1843 of Dartmoor granite, in the Corinthian order. Nelson himself stands on top, carved in sandstone by Edward Hodges Baily. The four bronze lions around the base, designed by Sir Edwin Landseer, arrived in 1867, some years after the column itself was finished.
